1.reason: a promotion over 1800s exceeds the service pass bound by design; the supervisor restart path is out of this section's scope

findings.text: wait_for_in_flight re-implements the join loop PromotionService.settle already carries at :419, so the class has two ways to wait for one thread list and a later change to one will diverge from the other; express settle in terms of it, and drop the timeout parameter no caller passes.

the join at :288 passes no timeout, so the plan's absolute never-killed-partway is bounded by SERVICE_PASS_BOUND_SECONDS: a promotion longer than 1800s is still stopped by the supervisor's restart at fleet_supervisor.py:1745-1749, a path the node's evidence does not cover.

test_a_draining_service_starts_no_request asserts started == [] after begin_drain(), an absence with no positive control, so it also passes when the request is never launchable at all, for example with the slot lease already held; it needs a no-drain arm asserting the same request does start.

tick() gained an early return that no gate arm measured on the file that exercises it, tests/test_no_caller_waits_on_a_promotion.py, which calls tick() throughout; the risk is low because _draining defaults to False, but the importing-tests arm did not run that file.
